STRUTTING

Hiring or Supplying Struts: Compare the Full Commercial Commitment

Look beyond the initial equipment rate when evaluating a support package.

In this insight

Understand what is being pricedTest the duration assumptionsExamine condition and return obligationsCompare alternatives on one basisFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Understand what is being priced

A support quotation may describe hire, supply, installation or an integrated package. These models transfer different obligations to the buyer. Request a clear schedule covering design, transport, fabrication, assembly, inspection, maintenance, modifications and return or disposal. The headline rate becomes useful only when the included work and the responsibility boundaries are understood.

Test the duration assumptions

Where charges depend on time, examine the start and end triggers. Is the period measured from delivery, installation or another agreed milestone? What happens if a later construction package delays release? The contract should explain extension rates and the process for documenting changes. A realistic duration scenario can reveal a materially different total from the initial short-period quotation.

Examine condition and return obligations

Clarify inspection records, ownership, permitted modifications and the condition expected at return. Identify responsibility for damaged, lost or altered components. These discussions should be linked to the planned work, not left as generic clauses that no one reads until demobilisation. Ensure the delivery team understands the agreed terms so site decisions do not accidentally create unexpected liabilities.

Compare alternatives on one basis

Prepare a whole-package comparison using the same programme assumptions and scope boundaries. Include foreseeable interfaces and clearly separate allowances from firm prices. If one proposal leaves important activities to others, add those activities to the comparison rather than treating the exclusion as a saving. The preferred offer should be commercially transparent and compatible with the approved engineering and delivery approach.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Compare hire, supply and installation scopes separately.
  • Model realistic duration changes.
  • Clarify modification and return obligations.
